title: Typewriter and Orchard
premise: In 1914 Kent, Cyrus Crane drives for suffragist Edith Marlowe and secretly reads the letters he delivers, memorizing lives he'll never have. When war breaks out, a sealed letter reveals that the Hollis family—German-born orchard keepers who once sheltered Edith—are to be interned as enemy aliens, and among their papers is a promise Cyrus made in peacetime: to protect their daughter Greta's inheritance and her letters to a dying brother. As suspicion falls on everyone who ever spoke kindly of the Hollises, Cyrus must choose between his duty to Edith's cause and the family no one will defend. The novel ends with Cyrus smuggling Greta and the orchard's deed to safety at terrible cost to his own invisibility—and with Edith choosing him over the movement that made her.
about_author: Theo Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing wartime correspondence in rural England. His fiction is drawn from the marginalia, unsent drafts, and half-burned letters he was never supposed to read.

chapters.title: The Weight of Paper
chapters.summary: Cyrus Crane, driver and reluctant letter-reader, introduces his philosophy: everything can be carried if you know its weight. POV: Cyrus. Emotional beat: wry detachment masking loneliness.

chapters.title: Marlowe House
chapters.summary: Cyrus delivers Edith Marlowe to a suffrage rally; her ferocity unsettles and fascinates him. He glimpses the Hollis orchard from the road. POV: Cyrus. Beat: first crack in his armor.

chapters.title: Greta at the Gate
chapters.summary: A flat tire strands Cyrus at the Hollis farm; Greta Hollis feeds him plums and talks about her brother's letters from Berlin. POV: Cyrus. Beat: unexpected warmth, the beginning of found family.

chapters.title: What the Letters Say
chapters.summary: Cyrus reads a batch of village mail and realizes how much of people's lives passes through his hands—including Greta's letters to her ailing brother Anton. POV: Cyrus. Beat: guilt sharpening into responsibility.

chapters.title: The Promise in Peacetime
chapters.summary: Anton, home briefly, asks Cyrus to look after Greta and the orchard papers 'whatever happens.' Cyrus, embarrassed, promises. POV: Cyrus. Beat: an oath given too lightly.

chapters.title: Summer's Last Deliveries
chapters.summary: Edith plans a autumn march; the village splits over it. Greta teaches Cyrus to graft apple stock. POV: alternating Cyrus/Greta. Beat: idyll before rupture.

chapters.title: Sarajevo
chapters.summary: News arrives of the Archduke's assassination. The village pub turns ugly toward 'foreigners.' Cyrus watches Greta shrink. POV: Cyrus. Beat: dread settling like weather.

chapters.title: Declarations
chapters.summary: War is declared. Edith pivots the movement toward war relief; Cyrus delivers telegrams reading names aloud to weeping households. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the world measured now in what must be carried away.

chapters.title: Enemy in the Parish Book
chapters.summary: The vicar crosses out German names in the parish register. Greta's family is formally listed as enemy aliens. POV: Greta. Beat: erasure begins.

chapters.title: The Sealed Letter
chapters.summary: Cyrus is handed an official sealed letter addressed to the Hollises. He reads it against every rule: internment orders, forty-eight hours. POV: Cyrus. Beat: horror—the promise comes due.

chapters.title: Forty-Eight Hours
chapters.summary: Cyrus warns the Hollises; Mr. Hollis refuses to flee, insisting on innocence. Greta begs Cyrus to hide the deed and her brother's letters. POV: Cyrus. Beat: duty and promise collide.

chapters.title: Edith's Choice
chapters.summary: Cyrus asks Edith to intervene publicly; she refuses—her cause cannot afford German sympathies. Their first real quarrel. POV: Edith. Beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: The Cart at Midnight
chapters.summary: Cyrus moves trunks, deeds, and letters to a locked shed behind Marlowe House while soldiers wait at the orchard gate. POV: Cyrus. Beat: quiet heroism, terror in routine gestures.

chapters.title: Internment
chapters.summary: The Hollises are taken. Greta, British-born, is permitted to stay but under watch. Cyrus stands in the crowd, invisible, hating it. POV: Greta. Beat: grief and abandonment.

chapters.title: The Empty Orchard
chapters.summary: Greta tends untended trees; villagers strip windfalls and worse. Cyrus helps her rebuild a broken fence at night. POV: alternating. Beat: two people building something together out of ruin.

chapters.title: Letters Unsent
chapters.summary: Greta writes to Anton, now trapped in Germany; Cyrus carries them nowhere, keeping them in his coat like contraband hearts. POV: Cyrus. Beat: tenderness deepening into love neither names.

chapters.title: Suspicion Falls
chapters.summary: A neighbor reports seeing Cyrus at the orchard by night. A constable questions him; Edith covers for him, at cost. POV: Edith. Beat: she protects him despite herself.

chapters.title: The Committee
chapters.summary: Edith's suffrage committee demands she denounce the Hollises publicly or lose funding for the relief work. POV: Edith. Beat: the movement becomes another cage.

chapters.title: What Invisibility Costs
chapters.summary: Cyrus reflects on a lifetime of being unseen—workhouse, service, silence—and realizes Greta has made him visible to himself. POV: Cyrus. Beat: interior turning point.

chapters.title: The Denunciation Drafted
chapters.summary: Edith writes the statement; Cyrus, delivering her correspondence, reads it and cannot leave it on the tray. POV: alternating. Beat: betrayal looming from both sides.

chapters.title: Burnt Edges
chapters.summary: Cyrus withholds the statement, claiming it was lost. Edith suspects but says nothing. Trust frays silently between them. POV: Cyrus. Beat: guilt as a second sealed letter.

chapters.title: Anton's Last Letter
chapters.summary: A Red Cross letter arrives: Anton is dying in a Berlin hospital. Greta collapses; Cyrus vows to get her reply through channels that barely exist. POV: Greta. Beat: time running out made literal.

chapters.title: Channels
chapters.summary: Cyrus works his network—a Quaker clerk, a sympathetic postmistress—to route Greta's letter. Each favor costs a secret. POV: Cyrus. Beat: hope built from small corruptions.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Soldiers search Marlowe House for 'enemy correspondence.' The shed nearly discovered; Cyrus moves the papers to the church crypt in a coffin. POV: Cyrus. Beat: peak dread, dark comedy of desperation.

chapters.title: Edith Finds Out
chapters.summary: Edith discovers Cyrus has been hiding the Hollis papers all along. Instead of exposing him, she burns her own denunciation draft. POV: Edith. Beat: her choice of conscience over career.

chapters.title: News from Berlin
chapters.summary: Word returns: Anton died before the letter arrived. Greta goes silent, working the orchard like penance. POV: Greta. Beat: grief without an address.

chapters.title: The Deed Questioned
chapters.summary: A land agent claims the orchard for the Crown under alien-property rules. The hidden deed is now the only thing standing. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the promise narrows to paper.

chapters.title: Village Tribunal
chapters.summary: A tribunal reviews Greta's status; neighbors testify both ways. Edith speaks for her publicly, spending her reputation. POV: Edith. Beat: public redemption, private fear.

chapters.title: Reprieve and Threat
chapters.summary: Greta is conditionally released—but the property seizure proceeds regardless. Cyrus realizes legal means are exhausted. POV: Cyrus. Beat: the last door closing.

chapters.title: Plans Made in the Dark
chapters.summary: Cyrus proposes moving Greta and the deed to Edith's aunt in Wales. Edith offers her motorcar and herself. Three conspirators around one kitchen table. POV: alternating. Beat: found family crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Night Watch
chapters.summary: Final night at the orchard; Greta grafts one last cutting to carry north. Cyrus and she finally speak their love plainly. POV: Greta. Beat: tenderness before the storm.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: The journey south; a checkpoint stop where Edith bluffs an inspector using her suffrage-organizer authority. POV: Edith. Beat: courage borrowed and repaid.

chapters.title: Betrayal
chapters.summary: The neighbor's son tips off authorities; soldiers intercept them at a junction. Cyrus is arrested; the deed seized. POV: Cyrus. Beat: climax begins—everything lost.

chapters.title: The Cell
chapters.summary: In custody, Cyrus refuses to name Edith or Greta. An old army clerk he once helped quietly misfiles his charge sheet. POV: Cyrus. Beat: kindness repaid across years.

chapters.title: Edith's Stand
chapters.summary: Edith goes to the magistrate, trading her public silence on internment policy for the charges' dismissal—her movement's elders never forgive her. POV: Edith. Beat: sacrifice completing her arc.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: The deed dispute reaches court; the Quaker clerk produces proof the orchard was held in Greta's mother's English name all along. POV: Cyrus. Beat: truth arriving through the postal system he served.

chapters.title: Orchard Restored
chapters.summary: Greta wins back the land. She plants Anton's name on a wooden marker among the trees. POV: Greta. Beat: mourning given soil.

chapters.title: What Edith Lost
chapters.summary: Edith's committee expels her; she finds she minds less than expected. She and Cyrus admit what the whole book has circled. POV: Edith. Beat: love chosen over duty, freely.

chapters.title: The First Harvest
chapters.summary: Autumn again: the three of them harvest the orchard together, sending apples to internees' families. Cyrus delivers letters still—but now he answers some. POV: Cyrus. Beat: full-circle warmth.

chapters.title: Carried Forward
chapters.summary: Years later, Cyrus reads a letter from a grown child of an internee thanking the unknown hands that helped. He weighs it, smiles, and carries it home to Edith and Greta. POV: Cyrus. Beat: resolution—memory, love, and family outlasting the orders.
